category: SEC Football — It Just Means More
prompt: What happened at the end of the 2013 Iron Bowl?
response:
The end of the 2013 Iron Bowl between the Auburn Tigers and the Alabama Crimson Tide features one of the most famous plays in college football history, widely known as the **"Kick Six."**

With exactly one second left in the game and the score tied at 28-28, Alabama attempted a game-winning 57-yard field goal. Because of the length of the kick, Auburn placed a player, defensive back Chris Davis, in the end zone in case the kick fell short. 

The kick, attempted by Alabama's freshman kicker Adam Griffith, did fall short. Chris Davis caught the ball just inches from the back of the end zone. With a convoy of blockers in front of him, Davis sprinted out of the end zone, navigated his way down the left sideline, and returned the kickoff 109 yards for a game-winning touchdown as time expired. 

Auburn won the game 34-28, securing the SEC West division title and advancing to the SEC Championship Game, while dealing a devastating blow to Alabama's national championship hopes.
